title: MOFA condemns China’s transnational repression; urges democratic partners to jointly resist authoritarian aggression and defend freedom and human rights
text:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) condemns in the strongest possible terms China’s employment of transnational repression and threats of violence to undermine the personal safety and freedom of speech of Taiwan nationals.

Recently, a Chinese national allegedly financed the surveillance of Taiwanese artist Huang Yi-hao and orchestrated a traffic accident to attack and discourage him from performing in public. The Chinese national was motivated by his dissatisfaction with Mr. Huang’s criticism of the Chinese Communist Party regime. China’s suspected involvement constitutes a malicious attempt to silence political discourse.

The Taiwan New Taipei District Prosecutors Office has charged five local individuals involved in the incident with various crimes, including attempted aggravated assault.

Democratic Taiwan will not tolerate attempts by foreign forces to silence its people through scare tactics and violent actions that compromise their personal safety. Freedom of speech forms a key cornerstone of every democratic society. No one should be subjected to violent retaliation for expressing criticism.

MOFA emphasizes that this incident highlights the fact that China is already engaging in transnational repression in democratic societies. By targeting individuals, it aims to cause a chilling effect and erode both freedom of expression and public discourse. The government of Taiwan will staunchly safeguard the nation’s sovereignty, democracy, the rule of law, and the safety of Taiwan nationals. It will also hold those committing related violations accountable in accordance with the law.

MOFA reiterates that the people’s right to express views and determine their future should be free from threats, intimidation, and coercion by foreign forces. The government’s respect for this right makes democratic Taiwan vastly different from authoritarian China.

MOFA calls on the international community to collectively recognize the threat posed by China’s transnational repression and exploitation of the openness and freedoms of democratic societies to engage in intimidation, infiltration, and violent coercion within their borders.

The ROC (Taiwan) will continue to deepen cooperation with like-minded nations, using information exchanges and related mechanisms to jointly counter transnational repression, protect people targeted by it, and hold the organizers and perpetrators thereof accountable. Democratic countries must work together to resist authoritarian aggression and ensure that people can live free from fear. (E)
